---
title: "School tertiles and minimum-risk grades"
subtitle: "5.8 · the public twelve-school CDE example"
description: "Fixed cuts and unrestricted three-grade reporting for a twelve-school chronic-absence example."
---

Two boundaries partition the posterior-mean order of twelve schools into a grade report. The display evaluates
this fixed report and compares it with the minimum-risk report over all assignments using at most three grades at
the same τ. Grade 1 states lower chronic absence under the supplied posterior. Boundary changes alter both the
number and identity of the stated directions. The comparison therefore separates a conventional grouping along one
order from optimisation over the full capped family, while preserving the same posterior and reporting loss.


## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Tertiles** splits the schools into three groups of four. It states 48 pairs, expects 1.829 wrong directions and has risk .082255; the browser optimum states 45 pairs with risk .063774.
- **Archived grades** puts the cuts after positions 3 and 9. These reproduce the archived three-grade report: 45 stated pairs and risk .063774. The relation-change table has no changed pairs.
- **One boundary** puts both controls at position 6. One distinct boundary gives two grades, 36 stated pairs and risk .091293.
- **Higher withholding cost** raises τ to .45. The optimum now states 47 pairs and has risk .143197. The changed-pair table identifies the resulting relation changes.

The cut positions describe a fixed report along one order. The comparison enumerates every report with at most three grades, including other orders. Its average-error bound belongs to that exact optimum at the displayed τ; it is not a per-pair certainty threshold for the tertiles. Reports can disclose different amounts while being evaluated under the same loss.

The dots and intervals summarize the supplied school posterior. A shared grade withholds directions and does not assert equal chronic-absence probabilities. Rows inside a grade remain in posterior-mean order for reading, with no additional reported comparisons.

Data: California Department of Education, 2026 California School Dashboard chronic absenteeism data, academic year 2025–26, as adapted in postrank 1.1.0 (`pr_case_cde`). This deliberately spread twelve-school teaching subset is conditional on a statewide prior fitted to 5,834 eligible schools; prior-estimation uncertainty is not propagated. CDE source conditions apply; the data are not relicensed, are provided as is without warranty, and imply no CDE endorsement.

The analysis concerns directional reporting of chronic absence within this subset. It neither computes Dashboard status-and-change colours nor establishes school quality, causal effects, statewide optimality or calibration. Shared grades do not imply equal absence probabilities.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## In postrank

The following call evaluates the fixed tertiles at τ .20 without model fitting or optimisation.

```r
library(postrank)
g <- pr_case_cde$reference$actions$observed_rate_tertiles
postrank_evaluate(g, pr_case_cde$input, weights = c(negative_chronic_absence = 1), tau = .2)[c("N", "E", "primary_risk")]
```
:::
